The default Cloudflare domain is inherited from Flowseal/tg-ws-proxy. It is convenient for testing, but it is a shared endpoint and can stop working at any time because Cloudflare limits simultaneous WebSocket connections.

For a long-term setup, add your own domain to Cloudflare, set SSL/TLS mode to Flexible, create the kws1/kws2/kws3/kws4/kws5/kws203 A records from the Flowseal instructions, and enter that domain in TgWsProxy settings.

TgWsProxy for Android runs a local SOCKS5 proxy for Telegram and routes supported MTProto traffic through WebSocket connections.

Current mobile network tests show a working path only through CF Proxy. If direct Telegram routes are blocked, use CF only: supported traffic will go through the configured Cloudflare domain instead of direct Telegram upstreams.

Cloudflare Proxy is an alternative free route for unavailable Telegram data centers. TgWsProxy uses WebSocket hosts in the form kws*.domain, where the default domain is taken from the Flowseal/tg-ws-proxy project.

The default domain is intended as a ready-to-test option. For regular use, replace it with your own Cloudflare domain because shared Cloudflare WebSocket limits can make the default endpoint unavailable.
This app is based on the Android fork by amurcanov and runtime ideas/code from Flowseal tg-ws-proxy. The original projects and license notes are kept in the repository.

TgWsProxy creates a local SOCKS5 proxy for Telegram and routes connections through Direct, Cloudflare Worker or CF proxy.

In Telegram, set SOCKS5:
Host: 127.0.0.1
Port: 1081
No username or password
Worker is a free fallback route through your own Cloudflare Worker.\nPaste only a domain like example.username.workers.dev

Auto is recommended.
Worker first — if Direct fails often.
CF first — if you have a working CF domain.
Worker only / CF only — strict modes.
Direct only — for tests.
The foreground notification shows proxy status. You can stop or reconnect from the notification. Android requires this notification while the proxy service is running.
Enter the Worker hostname without https:// or path.
Recommended. The route is selected automatically based on failure statistics and current network.

TgWsProxy runs locally on the device and does not send your settings to an app-owned server. Diagnostic reports may include domains, routes and log fragments. Enable domain masking before publishing reports.

1. Set proxy port (usually 1081).
2. Start TgWsProxy.
3. In Telegram add SOCKS5: 127.0.0.1:1081 without login/password.
4. Tap Apply in Telegram if available.
5. If Telegram does not connect, open diagnostics.
TgWsProxy listens on local SOCKS5. Telegram must connect to 127.0.0.1 and your chosen port. Avoid port conflicts with ByeDPI or other local proxies.
Auto is recommended. Worker first tries Worker then fallbacks. CF first tries CF proxy first. Worker only / CF only are strict. Direct only is for diagnostics.
Paste only the Worker hostname, for example example.username.workers.dev. Do not paste a full https:// URL with path.
CF proxy uses kws*.domain WebSocket hosts. Built-in and upstream domains are for testing; use your own domain for regular use.
Android requires a foreground notification while the proxy runs. You can make it compact or minimal, and control it from notification actions.

For regular use add your domain in Cloudflare (Flexible SSL) and create kws* A records per Flowseal instructions. Enter only the domain in TgWsProxy, without https:// or path.
